item.title: Aso Caldera Farm & Horse Riding — Guide
item.description: The wide, rolling grasslands of the Aso caldera — grazed by cattle and horses for centuries and kept open by traditional burning — are the perfect setting for farm experiences and horse riding. At ranches and farm parks around the caldera, visitors can ride horses across open pasture with the volcanic peaks as a backdrop, take pony rides, feed and meet cows, horses, sheep and other farm animals, and try hands-on activities like milking or butter-making.

item.title: Tottori Sand-Dune Melons & Farm Tours — Guide
item.description: The same free-draining sandy soil that forms the Tottori Sand Dunes is turned to advantage in the farms behind them, where the loose, sun-warmed sand and long sunshine hours produce unusually sweet fruit. Tottori’s sand-grown melons are its most prized crop, alongside sand-cultivated Rakkyo shallots, watermelons and grapes. Farm tours in the melon season let visitors see how crops are grown in the challenging sandy ground, learn about the region’s distinctive ‘sand agriculture’, and taste ripe Tottori melon — sweet, fragrant and best eaten within days of picking — at its early-summer peak.
